import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.RigidityLemma

/-!
# An abelian variety is commutative (Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.4)

The group law of an abelian variety is commutative. This is Milne, *Abelian
Varieties*, §I.1 Corollary 1.4, and it is a consequence of the Rigidity Lemma
via Corollary 1.2 (`av_regularMap_isHom_of_zero`, `RigidityLemma.lean`).

## The argument

The inversion morphism `inv : A ⟶ A` of a group object is *pointed*: it sends the
identity to the identity (`GrpObj.one_inv`). By Milne Corollary 1.2 — every
pointed regular map between abelian varieties is a homomorphism — inversion is
therefore a **homomorphism** of group objects.

A group in which `x ↦ x⁻¹` is a homomorphism is commutative: from
`(xy)⁻¹ = x⁻¹y⁻¹` and `(xy)⁻¹ = y⁻¹x⁻¹` one gets `x⁻¹y⁻¹ = y⁻¹x⁻¹`, and inverting
gives `yx = xy`. Applying this in each hom-group `Hom(X, A)` — which mathlib
already knows is a `Group` when `A` is a group object — and then instantiating at
`X := A ⊗ A` with the two projections yields the object-level statement
`(β_ A A).hom ≫ μ = μ`, i.e. `IsCommMonObj A`.

## Why this file exists

`IsCommMonObj A` is precisely the instance that
`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`'s `MonObj.powSum` requires: the `g`-fold sum
`(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` is formed in the *commutative* monoid
`(C^g ⟶ A)`, and its `S_g`-symmetry (`MonObj.powSum_perm`) is exactly the
commutativity of `A`'s group law. Before this file, the project's
abelian-variety hypothesis package (`[GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
[GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]`) did **not** yield `IsCommMonObj A` by
synthesis, so `powSum` could not be instantiated at an actual abelian variety.
`isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth` closes that gap, making the symmetrisation step
of Milne III.6.1 applicable to its intended target.

## Main results

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isMonHom_grpObj_inv` — inversion on an abelian variety is a
  homomorphism (Milne I.1.2 applied to the pointed map `inv`).
* `CategoryTheory.MonObj.mul_comm_hom_of_isMonHom_inv` — the group-theoretic step,
  in any cartesian monoidal category: if inversion is a homomorphism then every
  hom-group `Hom(X, A)` is commutative.
* `CategoryTheory.IsCommMonObj.of_hom_mul_comm` — commutativity of all hom-groups
  upgrades to `IsCommMonObj`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth` — **Milne I.1.4**: an
  abelian variety is a commutative group object.

## References

Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §I.1 Corollary 1.4 (and Corollary 1.2), pp. 5–7
(`references/abelian-varieties.pdf`). Blueprint: `chap:AbelianVarietyRigidity`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe v u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj

namespace CategoryTheory.MonObj

variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K]

/-- **If inversion is a homomorphism, every hom-group is commutative.**

Purely group-theoretic, in any cartesian monoidal category. Postcomposition with
`GrpObj.inv` is inversion in the hom-group `Hom(X, A)` (`Hom.inv_def`), so the
hypothesis says `(u * v)⁻¹ = u⁻¹ * v⁻¹` there. Since always
`(u * v)⁻¹ = v⁻¹ * u⁻¹`, inverting both sides of `u⁻¹ * v⁻¹ = v⁻¹ * u⁻¹` gives
commutativity. -/
theorem mul_comm_hom_of_isMonHom_inv {A : K} [GrpObj A]
    (hinv : IsMonHom (GrpObj.inv (X := A))) (X : K) (f g : X ⟶ A) :
    f * g = g * f := by
  have key : ∀ u v : X ⟶ A, (u * v) ≫ GrpObj.inv (X := A)
      = (u ≫ GrpObj.inv (X := A)) * (v ≫ GrpObj.inv (X := A)) := by
    intro u v
    rw [Hom.mul_def, Hom.mul_def, Category.assoc, hinv.mul_hom]
    simp [lift_map_assoc]
  have h1 := key f g
  rw [← Hom.inv_def, ← Hom.inv_def, ← Hom.inv_def] at h1
  -- `h1 : (f * g)⁻¹ = f⁻¹ * g⁻¹`; invert, using `(f * g)⁻¹ = g⁻¹ * f⁻¹`.
  have h2 : ((f * g)⁻¹)⁻¹ = (f⁻¹ * g⁻¹)⁻¹ := by rw [h1]
  simpa using h2

end CategoryTheory.MonObj

namespace CategoryTheory.IsCommMonObj

variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] [BraidedCategory K]

/-- **Commutativity of all hom-groups upgrades to `IsCommMonObj`.** Instantiate
hom-commutativity at `X := A ⊗ A` with the two projections: `fst * snd` is
`lift fst snd ≫ μ = μ`, while `snd * fst` is `lift snd fst ≫ μ`, and in a
cartesian monoidal category `lift snd fst` *is* the braiding. -/
theorem of_hom_mul_comm {A : K} [MonObj A]
    (hcomm : ∀ (X : K) (f g : X ⟶ A), f * g = g * f) : IsCommMonObj A := by
  constructor
  have h := hcomm (A ⊗ A) (fst A A) (snd A A)
  rw [Hom.mul_def, Hom.mul_def, lift_fst_snd, Category.id_comp] at h
  have hb : (β_ A A).hom = lift (snd A A) (fst A A) := by
    apply hom_ext <;> simp
  rw [hb, ← h]

end CategoryTheory.IsCommMonObj

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]

/-- **Inversion on an abelian variety is a homomorphism.** The inversion morphism
is pointed (`GrpObj.one_inv` : `η ≫ inv = η`), so Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.2
(`av_regularMap_isHom_of_zero`, a consequence of the Rigidity Lemma) applies. -/
theorem isMonHom_grpObj_inv {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible (A ⊗ A).hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType (A ⊗ A).hom]
    [IsReduced (A ⊗ A).left] :
    IsMonHom (GrpObj.inv (X := A)) :=
  av_regularMap_isHom_of_zero _ GrpObj.one_inv

/-- **Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.4 — an abelian variety is commutative.**

The group law of an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field is
commutative: `A` is a commutative group object, `IsCommMonObj A`.

The proof is Milne's: inversion is pointed, hence a homomorphism by Corollary 1.2
(`isMonHom_grpObj_inv`, resting on the Rigidity Lemma); a group whose inversion is
a homomorphism is commutative (`mul_comm_hom_of_isMonHom_inv`); and commutativity
of every hom-group is `IsCommMonObj` (`IsCommMonObj.of_hom_mul_comm`).

This supplies the instance that `MonObj.powSum` (`Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean`)
needs, so the `g`-fold sum `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` and its
`S_g`-symmetry become available at an actual abelian variety — the symmetrisation
step of Milne III.6 Proposition 6.1.

Deliberately **not** an `instance`: the three `(A ⊗ A)`-side hypotheses are not
derived by synthesis from the abelian-variety package here, so consumers thread it
explicitly (`letI := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth (A := A)`), matching the
convention used for `Pic0.jacobianScheme_grpObj` in `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean`. -/
theorem isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible (A ⊗ A).hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType (A ⊗ A).hom]
    [IsReduced (A ⊗ A).left] :
    IsCommMonObj A :=
  IsCommMonObj.of_hom_mul_comm
    (MonObj.mul_comm_hom_of_isMonHom_inv isMonHom_grpObj_inv)

end AlgebraicGeometry

3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.

6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22

24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:

27	  another team.

29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,

36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`

223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
281	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
282	  as **memory**.
283	
284	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
285	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
286	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
287	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
288	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
289	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
290	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
291	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
292	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
293	
294	## Resuming after an interruption
295	
296	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
297	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
298	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
299	
300	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
301	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
302	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
303	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
304	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
305	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
306	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
307	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
308	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
309	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
310	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
311	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
312	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
313	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
314	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
315	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
316	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
317	
318	## Final report (your last message)
319	
320	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
321	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
322	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
323	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
324	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
325	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
326	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
327	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
328	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
329	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
330	not by itself a reason to stop.
331

333	
334	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
335	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
336	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
337	`subagents` skill):
338	
339	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
340	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
341	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
342	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
343	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
344	
345	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

SUMMARY: Construct picardJacobianWitness from Picard representability, the Pic0 abelian-variety structure, dimension g, and the Albanese universal property; discharge the protected Jacobian interface.  The structure is built and wired: the witness IS Scheme.Pic0Scheme, and 98 modules are reachable from the headline. What remains is mathematics, not assembly, so this item stays open with its only child done -- that status mismatch is deliberate.  FIVE OBLIGATIONS, measured with scripts/axiom-frontier.lean rather than asserted: Pic0.smooth and Pic0.proper are sorry-bodied upstream, and three leaves are stated at the headline. Their distances to the landed tree are now unequal and known:  - LEAF C (Albanese) is the closest. isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed is a THEOREM: over an algebraically closed field, in positive genus, and given the basepoint condition, the universal property is Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property applied with no transport. So leaf C adds exactly three things -- arbitrary base field (cluster G descent), genus zero (Mumford rigidity), and the basepoint condition P o iota_P = eta. The third is the one easily overlooked: it is a conjunct of IsAlbanese that the landed theorem never states, and it cannot be discharged before Pic0.abelJacobi is constructed, since it is a statement about that morphism.  - LEAF A (rational point) is not a distance at all: the statement is FALSE, so it must be replaced by whichever branch the owner picks in I-0372, never proved.  - LEAF B (dimension refinement) now has its landed half at the headline too, and it is NOT the dimension count. finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus proves dim T_e Pic0 = genus C by Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne with no transport, since genus C is definitionally dim_k H^1(C,O_C). An earlier summary called this missing mathematics with no bridge; that was retracted (memory I-0446).  Pic0.smooth and Pic0.proper belong to no current task and are the nearest unowned work under the headline.

SUMMARY: The headline rests on the infrastructure it claims, and every number here is measured rather than asserted. picardJacobianWitness is built from Scheme.Pic0Scheme, so 98 of the project's modules are reachable from Jacobian.lean rather than the 8 of the Genus-only import; the 98th arrived when leaf C was stated against the landed Albanese universal property, which put the Albanese cone under the headline for the first time.

EVERY MODULE ON DISK IS ROOTED at AlgebraicJacobian.lean -- 187 of 187 as of 2026-07-28, no exceptions. ONE CONVENTION FOR THE DENOMINATOR, since the two figures in this node count differently and Ground flagged it: 187 is the number of .lean files UNDER AlgebraicJacobian/, excluding the root aggregator AlgebraicJacobian.lean itself, which is the seed rather than a member. Both '187 of 187 rooted' and '98 of 187 reachable from the headline' use that same 187, so they are comparable; the tree contains 188 files if you count the root. which matters because an unrooted module compiles green and is invisible BOTH to the root build and to the axiom probe: #print axioms on its declarations cannot even be written against the root import. The standing check is in the probe header and in I-0388. A module not yet committed to the ledger must NOT be rooted (a clean checkout would fail); that grace period ends at the commit.

THE OBLIGATION COUNT IS FIVE, over a general base field AND over an algebraically closed one. The count does not drop when leaf A is discharged; only the KIND of the obligations changes. The five: instHasPicScheme, Pic0.smooth and Pic0.proper (sorry-bodied upstream), and leaves B and C stated at the headline -- with leaf A a sixth over a general field, where it is the FALSE one. Each leaf's distance to the landed tree is COMPILER-CHECKED rather than described, by a companion theorem stated at the headline:

  leaf A (rational point) -- FALSE over a general k, so it must be REPLACED, not proved. Over an algebraically closed field it is a THEOREM: hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed is axiom-clean via Albanese.hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed, and picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed assembles the witness with it supplied rather than assumed. This bounds I-0372's decision without choosing a branch: what is undecided is what the project claims over an ARBITRARY base field.
  instHasPicScheme (representability) -- the obligation that is easy to miscount. Scheme.Pic0Scheme carries [HasPicScheme C] and this sorry-bodied instance is its sole producer. Over a general field the gate is reached THROUGH leaf A, so counting it separately looks like double-counting; discharging leaf A makes it FIRE rather than removing it, so over k-bar it stands free.
  leaf B -- owes Pic0.smooth plus the passage from a tangent-space dimension to Mathlib's presentation-based SmoothOfRelativeDimension; the dimension count itself is landed (finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus proves dim T_e Pic0 = genus C with no transport).
  leaf C -- one basepoint condition plus two generalizations away (isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed proves the algebraically closed positive-genus case).

WHY THE KIND OF OBLIGATION MATTERS AND CANNOT BE READ OFF THE PROBE: over k-bar all five are unproved TRUE statements; leaf A over a general field is FALSE, so the general witness rests on an inconsistent hypothesis and its consequences are vacuously true. Both states report exactly the same sorryAx, so the distinction has to be exhibited by a discharge rather than measured. That is why the alg-closed witness is a separate definition.

theorem existsUnique_hom_of_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] [Y.IsSeparated]
    (f : X.RationalMap Y) (h : indeterminacyLocus f = ∅) :
    ∃! (g : X ⟶ Y), g.toRationalMap = f := by
  -- The domain of definition is all of `X`.
  have hdom : f.toPartialMap.domain = ⊤ := by
    rw [toPartialMap_domain, ← TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_inj,
      TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_top, ← Set.compl_empty_iff]
    exact h
  -- The candidate morphism: transport the maximal representative along
  -- `X ≅ ⊤ ≅ f.toPartialMap.domain`.
  have hwit : (X.topIso.inv ≫ X.homOfLE hdom.ge
      ≫ f.toPartialMap.hom).toRationalMap = f := by
    conv_rhs => rw [← f.toRationalMap_toPartialMap]
    refine PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mpr ?_
    refine ⟨⊤, by rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.coe_top]; exact dense_univ,
      le_top, hdom.ge, ?_⟩
    simp only [PartialMap.restrict_hom, Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap,
      Scheme.topIso_hom, Scheme.ι_toIso_inv_assoc,
      Scheme.homOfLE_homOfLE_assoc]
  exact ⟨_, hwit, fun g hg => hom_ext_of_toRationalMap_eq (hg.trans hwit.symm)⟩
